cases.persona: Riley, a plan with a deposit and the first payment today, in a short month (invented, D-63, D-65, Plan-49 re-run)
cases.situation: November so far: $2,500 in on the 1st, bills $1,500 paid, $650 spent. On 15 November 2026 Riley has $5,000 in her everyday account (money from earlier months) and her safety net holds $2,000, its full size, locked (the default). She looks at a $9,000 car on a 48-month plan at 7.9% with a $500 deposit, the first payment due today, 15 November 2026. A usual month: pay $2,500 on the 1st, bills $1,500 and everyday spending $1,300 ($700 of it on essentials), so it ends $300 short.
cases.why: Her usual month is already $300 short, so a new monthly payment cannot fit: "Short each month", with the headline "No: your month is already short" (D-63; a plan payment makes the month more short, so it is D-65's Large tier) and no ready-by date. The $8,500 left after the deposit is paid off in 48 payments of $205.76 (the last $205.57), the first of them today. The plan's total is the deposit plus every payment, each counted once (Plan-49 re-run: the payment due today is one of the 48, not an extra one): $500 + 47 x $205.76 + $205.57 = $10,376.29, so it costs $1,376.29 in interest, money that could stay with her. The day-one cost ($500 + $205.76) comes from her $4,350 of spare money. The depletion lines show (D-54): the $205.76 payment takes the usual month from $300 short to $505.76 short, the $9,000 price is more than her $2,000 safety net, and $300 a month in lower costs or higher income balances the month; the net is locked, so no line says how long it would last (D-61, D-66).
